title: Four-Kernel Classification for 2-Connected Cycle Rank Three
Exact Branch-Kernel Relation Reduction
statement:
Let a finite fiber-coherence CSP have a tree-absorbed 2-connected
incidence block. Suppress each maximal degree-two path. Give every
remaining branch node its surviving state domain. For every kernel edge
e, let R_e be the binary relation of branch-state pairs extendable
through its suppressed path. Then the original block has a coherent
section if and only if the binary CSP on the branch kernel with edge
relations R_e has a solution.

title: K4-Free Arbitrary Binary-Relation Strip
statement:
For finite sets A,B and any relation R subset A x B, there is a finite
K4-free stable-partition graph gadget with boundary fibers X indexed by
A and Y indexed by B such that a boundary choice (a,b) extends to a
coherent section of the gadget if and only if (a,b) belongs to R. The
gadget has four realized triangle types arranged in a path.

title: Complete-Graph Coloring Core
statement:
For every integer q at least 2, the binary CSP with q+1 variables,
domain [q], and inequality on every pair of variables is inclusion-minimal
incoherent. Its binary constraint graph is K_(q+1), with cycle rank
q(q-1)/2.

title: Universal K4-Free Realization of Finite Binary CSPs
statement:
Every finite binary CSP has a polynomial-size realization as the exact
boundary projection of a finite K4-free fiber-coherence system. One
stable boundary fiber represents each CSP variable, and one private
R3K03 strip represents each binary constraint.

title: NP-Completeness of Finite K4-Free Fiber Coherence
statement:
Given a finite K4-free graph together with its stable partition and
realized triangle-type fiber system, deciding whether a coherent section
exists is NP-complete. NP-hardness holds with branch domains of size
three.

title: Q4 Kernel Intersection Criterion
statement:
For the four-parallel-edge kernel Q4 with branch domains S,T and path
relations R1,R2,R3,R4 subset S x T, coherence is equivalent to
R1 intersect R2 intersect R3 intersect R4 being nonempty.

title: Doubled-Square Kernel Reduction
statement:
For the D22 kernel, intersect each doubled opposite edge pair to obtain
relations P and Q. Orient the two remaining single relations S,T around
the resulting four-cycle. The block is coherent if and only if the
composition P o S o Q o T contains a fixed point.

title: Doubled-Triangle Kernel Join Criterion
statement:
For the T221 kernel with branch nodes A,B,C, let P be the intersection
of the two A-B relations, Q the intersection of the two A-C relations,
and T the B-C relation. The block is coherent if and only if there exist
a,b,c with P(a,b), Q(a,c), and T(b,c).

title: K4 Kernel Exact CSP Criterion
statement:
For the simple K4 branch kernel with branch domains D1,D2,D3,D4 and six
edge relations R_ij, coherence is equivalent to the existence of
(x1,x2,x3,x4) in the domain product satisfying R_ij(xi,xj) for every
pair i<j.

title: Complete Cycle-Rank-Three Structural Classification
Polynomial-Time Fixed-Rank-Three Coherence
statement:
Finite fiber coherence on a tree-absorbed 2-connected incidence block of
cycle rank at most three is decidable, with a section or exact failure
certificate, in polynomial time in the explicit relation-table size.

title: Intrinsic K4 Pigeonhole Core on Three Colors
statement:
The K4-kernel CSP with four variables, domain {0,1,2}, and inequality on
all six edges is inclusion-minimal incoherent. Every relation is fully
supported, and every one-edge-deleted rank-two subblock is coherent.

title: Domain Three Is Minimal for the K4 Pigeonhole Core
statement:
The intrinsic K4 inequality mechanism of R3K13 cannot be inclusion-minimal
on a two-element domain, while a three-element domain suffices.

title: K4-Free Realization of the Intrinsic K4 Core
statement:
There is a finite K4-free stable-partition graph whose fiber-coherence
projection is the intrinsic three-color K4 kernel of R3K13. It has no
coherent section, while deleting any one complete relation-strip block
restores coherence.

title: Exact First- and Second-Order Deletion Profile of the K4 Core
Pair-Deletion Profile Reconstructs the Constraint Geometry
statement:
In the R3K13 core, the pair-deletion number D_ef equals 12 exactly when
constraint edges e,f share a K4 endpoint, and equals 18 exactly when they
are disjoint. Hence the second-order deletion profile reconstructs the
line graph L(K4), and therefore the full adjacency geometry of the six
constraint blocks.

title: Exact Violation Ledger of the Three-Color K4 Core
statement:
Among the 3^4=81 assignments of the R3K13 core, the numbers violating
j inequality constraints are
N_0=0, N_1=36, N_2=18, N_3=24, N_6=3,
and N_j=0 otherwise.

title: General Complete-Graph Core Deletion Formulas
Second-Order Repair Is the First Noncollapsed Geometric Invariant
statement:
Scalar extension slack and the complete one-step repair matrix are
universal on inclusion-minimal incoherent cores, but the pair-deletion
profile need not collapse: in the first intrinsic rank-three core it
recovers whether two constraints are adjacent or disjoint.

title: Fixed-Cycle-Rank Tractability versus Unbounded NP-Completeness
statement:
Let r be fixed and d bound every fiber domain. Finite fiber coherence on
incidence graphs of cyclomatic number at most r is decidable in
O(d^r poly(N)) time. In contrast, without a cycle-rank bound the problem
is NP-complete even for K4-free graph realizations with domain size three.

title: Refined Finite-Fiber #595 Close Split through Rank Three
statement:
For every stable finite-fiber compression of a hypothetical Erdős #595
witness, one of the following holds:
1. a finite incoherence core has incidence cycle rank at most three and
   is exactly certified by the forest, unicyclic, theta/cactus, or R3K11
   algorithms;
2. a finite minimal core has cycle rank at least four;
3. every finite subsystem coheres and compactness gives a full coherent
   section, yielding an exact uncountably chromatic Berge-C3-free
   hypergraph compression.

title: Rank-Four Branch-Kernel Census Target
statement:
Enumerate the loopless 2-connected multigraph branch kernels of
cyclomatic number four, reduce every subdivided block to its exact binary
kernel CSP, and classify which topologies collapse to parallel
intersection, monodromy, cactus gluing, or complete-graph coloring
mechanisms. For the first intrinsic rank-four cores, compute the full
pair-deletion geometry and compare it with the complete-graph family.

title: Higher-Order Repair Reconstruction Target
statement:
For a minimal finite incoherent core C, form the hierarchy
D_S=|Sol(C-S)| for deletion sets S of size two and three, retaining the
incidence locations of S. Determine the least order at which this repair
hierarchy reconstructs the branch kernel for every core of fixed cycle
rank four, and identify nonisomorphic cores with identical lower-order
profiles.
